overview: A late payment clause specifies the consequences when Tenant fails to pay Rent by the due date. It typically includes (a) a grace period before the payment is considered late, (b) a late charge expressed as a flat fee or percentage of the unpaid amount (most commonly 5%), and (c) an interest rate applied to delinquent amounts. Many leases waive the first late charge per 12-month period if Tenant cures within a short window after written notice.
preliminary: OTHER LEASE CLAUSES – MASTER ABSTRACTION GUIDE
General Applicability: All leases (Office, Retail and Industrial).

questions.question_text: Does the lease contain a Late Payment Charge or late fee clause (keywords: 'late charge', 'late payment charge', 'late fee', or a stated percentage of delinquent amount)?
questions.extraction_hint: Extract full clause including: (a) grace period in days, (b) late fee amount or %, (c) any first-late-waiver provision, (d) any default interest rate on overdue sums.
questions.notes: Default location: Section 3 (HMBP-BCP leases) or Paragraph 4 (ProLogis leases).

questions.question_text: What is the late fee amount or percentage?
questions.extraction_hint: Extract the dollar amount or percentage (e.g., '5%' or '$100').

questions.question_text: What is the grace period (number of days after due date before late charge applies)?
questions.extraction_hint: Extract the number of days, e.g., '7 days', '10 days'.
